transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-09 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sara Patel (Redwood AE), Tom Nguyen (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair (Helix Medical), Alex Romero (Helix Eng), Maya Chen (Helix Security)

[00:00:00] Sara: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm sara from redwood, i'll kick us off. we have about 40 minutes, we'll do a quick intro, a short hosted api walkthrough — chat and text generation basics — and then leave time for q&a.
[00:00:15] Priya: great, thanks. quick context: we're building a clinical notes summarization assistant and triage helper, latency target ~300ms token for short prompts, throughput of ~200 requests/minute. security is big for us.
[00:00:30] Sara: perfect, that's helpful. tom will run through the demo and show streaming and param controls.
[00:00:40] Tom: hi all, i'll share my screen, give a quick overview of the hosted api endpoints, then live demo with streaming responses. apologies if the demo has a bit of stutter, i'm on wifi.
[00:01:05] Tom: so the basic call is POST /v1/chat/completions, or /v1/text/generate for single-turn; body includes model, messages or prompt, and params like temperature, top_p, max_tokens, top_k if you want. default safety and moderation hooks are applied server-side.
[00:01:30] Alex: do we have client SDKs or is REST preferred?
[00:01:35] Tom: both — we have SDKs for python/node/go and a simple curl example. streaming is via server-sent events over the same endpoint to reduce latency for token-by-token delivery. i'll show python streaming in a sec.
[00:02:00] [screen share starts]
[00:02:10] Tom: demo snippet: create client, call chat.create with stream=True, iterate over chunks. note: streaming reduces end-to-end latency because you don't wait for full decode. for your 300ms target, streaming plus small max_tokens per turn helps.
[00:02:30] Priya: how does that interact with kv cache or long context? we have long patient histories up to 16k tokens.
[00:02:45] Tom: good q; hosted api supports larger context models we surface in the model catalog. we also use prefix caching and the runtime uses kv cache to avoid recomputing past keys when doing multi-turns — for very long contexts we recommend our chunking pattern or embeddings+retrieval to keep latency predictable. slight transcription: i said "kv cache" but sometimes the export shows "k v cash" ha.
[00:03:10] Maya: from security side: do you store PII? how's retention?
[00:03:20] Sara: hosted api by default retains logs for 30 days for debugging; enterprise customers can opt out or use Redwood Private/dedicated where control plane and retention is different. we also offer KMS integration for encrypting customer data at rest.
[00:03:40] Maya: do you have SOC2 docs?
[00:03:44] Sara: yes, we'll share our SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs, plus the security one-pager after the call. link: (internal) https://redwood.example.com/security-brief
[00:03:58] Tom: jumping back to params: temperature influences randomness; for clinical summarization you'd likely use temperature 0 - 0.2 and lower top_p. set max_tokens to cap length, and use stop sequences for structured outputs. also we support function-calling/structured responses if you want JSON outputs.
[00:04:30] Priya: can you show retries/backoff if the api returns 500 or rate limited? we need deterministic retry guidance.
[00:04:45] Tom: yes — best practice: implement exponential backoff with jitter, avoid retrying on 4xx (except 429 which should be retried after Retry-After header). our SDKs have a retry helper. for streaming calls, you need to re-open stream and use the conversation id to re-request missing tokens or re-generate last segment — we demonstrate in the sample. i'll paste that.
[00:05:15] Tom: quickly showing curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"rw-medium-16k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize..."}],"max_tokens":150,"temperature":0.1}' 
[00:05:40] Alex: what about rate limits and quotas? if we start at 200 req/min that's small but bursty.
[00:05:50] Sara: hosted api rate limits are per API key; for prod we can provision higher quotas or recommend dedicated capacity. we also have token-level billing. for bursts we suggest client-side rate limiting plus Redwood's token bucket; we can configure burst windows for the account.
[00:06:10] Priya: curious about latency SLOs — do you publish typical p50/p95 numbers?
[00:06:20] Tom: yes on the console we show per-route p50/p95 token latencies. typical p95 for rw-medium-16k on NVidia A100s is ~180ms per token for plain generation, but real numbers depend on sequence length, batching, and quantization. we'll share benchmark sheets.
[00:06:45] Maya: what about HIPAA / PHI handling for hosted?
[00:06:50] Sara: hosted can be ok if you sign a BAA and opt into minimal retention; for strict PHI we often recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with customer-managed networking and KMS. we'll include BAA next steps.
[00:07:10] [demo: streaming python snippet shown]
[00:07:25] Tom: note: in streaming we yield interim chunks, and you can choose to display partial tokens to users. the SDK surfaces chunk.type = 'delta' and chunk.content. also if connection drops we provide chunk.continuation tokens to resume in some cases — there's edge cases, so we recommend short-lived increments and checkpointing conversation ids.
[00:08:00] Priya: how do you handle hallucinations or unexpected model output? do you provide guardrails?
[00:08:10] Tom: we have built-in moderation filters and recommend prompt engineering with system instructions and post-processing checks. Redwood Optimize also provides evals and quality monitoring so you can alert on regressions tied to prompt sets.
[00:08:35] Alex: for POC, can we run a benchmark on our sample dataset and get per-token cost estimates?
[00:08:45] Sara: yes; typically we run a 1-week POC where we run your sample prompts through hosted endpoints and report latency/cost. if you want isolation we can do Dedicated.
[00:09:00] Tom: about retries again — when you see 503 or 504 that's usually transient, back off with exponential jitter starting at 200ms up to a few seconds; for 429, check Retry-After and also consider client-side token bucket to smooth spikes. the SDK automatically retries idempotent requests.
[00:09:30] Priya: sounds good. any docs for best-effort client patterns? circuit breakers, streaming resume?
[00:09:40] Tom: yes i'll send a guide. sample pattern: maintain conversation state, checkpoint last confirmed token index, on reconnect re-issue request with messages up to last confirmed, set stream=true, then discard overlap. it's described in our streaming-resume.md in the docs.
[00:10:10] Maya: audit logs / events are they available? we need immutable audit trails.
[00:10:18] Sara: yes, console offers request-level logs, and enterprise plans include longer retention and export to your SIEM. we'll share the docs.
[00:10:30] [00:10:30]
[00:10:35] Tom: quick sample run: i'll send a prompt -> we'll get tokens streaming in — (stream plays) — you can see partial sentences arrive at 80-120ms intervals. this is simulated in demo, real env may vary.
[00:11:10] Priya: any gotchas with concurrency limits on single connection?
[00:11:18] Tom: single connection is fine, but browsers have limits on concurrent open SSE connections. for high concurrency use server-side pooling or multiplexing.
[00:11:35] Alex: for cost, what's the biggest lever?
[00:11:40] Sara: model choice, quantization, batching, and caching. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles, batching strategies and reuse of cached prefixes to cut token compute. we can show estimated savings in the cost worksheet.
[00:12:05] Priya: what models are in the catalog and how do you handle version pinning?
[00:12:12] Tom: model catalog includes open models (gpt-like, rw-family), and we support pinning specific model versions for routes so your prod traffic isn't affected by new model rollouts. rollouts can be canary or A/B.
[00:12:35] Priya: ok, timeline: we want a POC in 2 weeks.
[00:12:40] Sara: we'll aim to schedule bench week of 2026-05-19. I'll email days and request your sample prompts and security contact.
[00:12:55] Maya: do you support SSO and RBAC for the console?
[00:13:00] Sara: yes SAML/SSO, fine-grained RBAC and audit logs. we'll include setup guide.
[00:13:20] Tom: small technical note: for streaming with long context, ensure you trim system messages and use retrieval for large archives; otherwise latency can spike. also watch KV cache eviction settings if you're switching models.
[00:13:45] Priya: where do retries impact billing? if we re-request tokens are we billed twice?
[00:13:55] Sara: billing is per token decoded/generated; if you reissue a request that regenerates tokens you'll be billed for the new tokens. so smart retries and idempotency are important. we can help design checkpointing to minimize duplicate generation.
[00:14:20] Alex: for the POC we'll likely start on hosted and then move to Dedicated if we need stricter isolation.
[00:14:30] Sara: that's common. Dedicated gives reserved capacity and lower variability for latency; hosted is easiest to get started.
[00:14:45] Priya: ok can you send the checklist for production readiness? compliance, BAA, perf testing?
[00:14:50] Sara: yes we'll send a production checklist.
[00:15:00] [Q&A continues with small clarifications about SDKs and websocket vs SSE]
[00:20:00] Tom: one last demo note — for streaming resilience we recommend chunk sizes of 16-64 tokens, and use the conversation id to correlate; for very low latency use shorter generation windows.
[00:25:00] Priya: thanks — this was helpful.
[00:25:10] Sara: recap: we'll share pricing, security docs, streaming examples, and schedule the POC. any other blockers?
[00:25:20] Priya: need to confirm budget and legal (BAA).
[00:25:30] Maya: will review SOC2 and confirm retention options.
[00:25:40] Alex: i'll prepare sample prompts and send by May 12.
[00:26:00] Sara: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with attachments and a calendar invite for POC week.
[00:26:15] [call ends]

Notes: occasional transcription glitches (names, product variants like "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Dedicated"), filler words, and short crosstalk were left intact to preserve realism. Links/attachments referenced: security one-pager, pricing sheet, streaming-resume.md, benchmark spreadsheet.
